items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 for ambitious technical work
facts: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision.
They generate outputs up to 30% faster than Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, and they’re available at a lower price: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.

During prerelease testing they’ve helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours.

x_posts.author: @claudeai
x_posts.text:
Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges.

They’re capable collaborators on ambitious projects in many fields, and show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision.

x_posts.author: @claudeai
x_posts.text:

Read more: https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.321 makes Claude Fable 5.2 the default Fable model
facts: Added Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), now the default Fable model — 1M context, $8/$40 per Mtok with $0.20/Mtok cache reads.
Added --settings <file> to claude remote-control, which applies a settings file to every session it starts.

x_posts.author: @nxtday
x_posts.text:
Anthropic just made Claude Fable 5.2 the default Fable model in Claude Code. 🚀

Per Anthropic's Nov 9 post, Fable 5.2 is live on paid plans and major clouds. Outputs run up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1, and API pricing is $8 input and $40 output per million tokens, down from $10 and $50.

Claude Code changelog 2.1.321 (Nov 9) adds Fable 5.2 with a 1M context window as the default Fable model.

On FrontierCode 2.0 at Xhigh effort, Anthropic reports Fable 5.2 at 49.1%, ahead of Opus 5.5 at 45.5%.

Image: Anthropic

@nxtday take: The rumor was 5.5. The ship was 5.2. Ship beats rumor.

Fable for hard agent work or stick with Opus daily? 🤔

items.title: Developers discuss multi-model advisor setups for Claude Code with Fable 5.2
facts: The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5 at once, each one doing only the job it's best at.
You just launch Claude Code like this: claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

x_posts.author: @xsmryze
x_posts.text:
THIS IS AN ACTUAL F*CKING GOLDMINE

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5 at once, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Better results and way fewer tokens, because every task lands on the right model.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session, writes the code and applies the fixes
→ Haiku 5.5 swarms the repo in parallel: search, grep and diff audits
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls and signs off on the diff
→ you stop burning Opus context on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku swarms. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and coordinates the work
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5, read-only
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5 in its own context
> audit checks the diff on Haiku 5.5 in a throwaway worktree
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reviews the synthesized diff before sign-off
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Reconfigure my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three Haiku 5.5 subagents in .claude/agents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), audit (checks the diff).
3. Set isolation: worktree on audit so its checks never touch my working branch.
4. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: delegate every repo search and test run to the Haiku 5.5 subagents to keep the main context small.
5. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff…

items.title: Open-source projects enable AI agents to control real phones
facts: Three open source projects hit GitHub this week that let it tap through a real phone.
Pinky - Claude Code, Codex or Cursor drive your iPhone or Android while you watch, payments wait for your click.

x_posts.author: @Alexvx_nft
x_posts.text:
YOUR AI AGENT CAN USE YOUR PHONE NOW

Three open source projects hit GitHub this week that let it tap through a real phone

PHONE

1. Pinky - Claude Code, Codex or Cursor drive your iPhone or Android while you watch, payments wait for your click
http://github.com/DIYgod/pinky

2. Poki - operates a real iPhone through a local MCP server, no jailbreak, a free Apple account works
http://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki

3. phoneuse - a Linux PC sees your iPhone over AirPlay and taps as a Bluetooth mouse, no app on the phone, still a tech demo
http://github.com/lxe/phoneuse

MAKE

4. sand3d - 3D objects as short Python, a washing machine with a working door in 38 lines
http://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d

5. vork - the agent writes the scene and its own shaders as code, then renders on the GPU
http://github.com/voyager-so/vork

6. cinecode - runs inside Claude Code or Cursor, writes the script, builds every frame in code and hands you an MP4
http://github.com/sarpstar/cinecode

CHECK

7. Neoverse - free to search, risk verdicts on 4M+ MCP servers, skills and extensions
http://verse.neo.ai

While sorting by stars I also hit five new repos created within the same hour, 478 to 480 stars each and almost no forks

One calls itself a pre-activated Claude toolkit

Don't install anything on stars alone

Pinky is my pick, its approvals sit in the gateway so the agent can't just ignore them

Would you let an agent touch your real phone ?
